newsitem.title: USA: House Republican favors tobacco tax for kids health.
newsitem.headline: House Republican favors tobacco tax for kids health.

text.p: A senior House Republican said Monday she would introduce a bill to provide health coverage for 5 million uninsured children, funded by a 43-cents-per-pack boost in the federal cigarette tax.

Connecticut Republican Rep. Nancy Johnson announced she would sponsor a childrens' health bill, virtually identical to a bipartisan measure introduced in the Senate by Massachusetts Democrat Edward Kennedy and Utah Republican Orrin Hatch.

The legislation would give states grants to provide health care to about half of the estimated 10 million U.S. children without insurance. The program would be funded by raising the federal cigarette tax to 67 cents per pack from the current level of 24 cents.
"Millions of American families are working hard, paying taxes and playing by the rules, yet their children do not have health insurance," Johnson said in a statement.
Johnson is on the powerful House Ways and Means Committee, which has jurisdiction over the issue.

The legislation is the latest in a slew of bills that have been introduced in Congress on the topic. Senate Democrats have said that providing insurance to children is their No. 1 health priority this year.
President Clinton's balanced budget plan calls for covering as many as 5 million children, mainly by expanding access to the Medicaid insurance program for the poor and disabled.

Republican leaders have said they want to address the issuse, but are looking for a market-oriented approach, rather than a government mandate. Many Republican leaders also oppose any effort to raise the federal tobacco tax.
